summary: Add a worked gas-volume balance and focused reverse-stoichiometry practice to round out an otherwise strong chapter.

improvements.where: note, after the existing worked example; pack worked
improvements.why: The current worked examples start from solution volumes, while the syllabus explicitly includes gas volumes in combustion and the note warns about condensed water without demonstrating a full final-gas calculation.
improvements.what: Add a step-by-step combustion example with a stated starting oxygen volume at r.t.p.: balance the equation, identify the oxygen consumed, calculate oxygen remaining and carbon dioxide formed, exclude liquid water at r.t.p., and sum the final gas volumes. Add a parallel faded version with different data; retain all existing examples.

improvements.why: The outcome asks learners to deduce stoichiometric relationships from measured quantities; current generated reverse practice is a single simple acid-to-gas ratio item.
improvements.what: Add one multi-step structured item that infers an unknown coefficient ratio from measured solution amounts and gas volume, and one exam-style numeric or MCQ item that deduces a formula or reaction ratio from reacting mass and gas volume. Give each full working, three graduated hints, and significant-figure handling.
